newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin begins forced repatriation of Bosnians.
newsitem.headline: Berlin begins forced repatriation of Bosnians.

text.p: Berlin authorities began the forcible repatriation of Bosnian refugees on Thursday as police accompanied two Bosnian men to Sarajevo, via Zurich and Zagreb.

The Berlin Interior Authorities said one of the men was a convicted criminal and the other was one of the group of people -- including single adults and married couples without children -- who are obliged to leave the country first.
Germany plans to send 90,000 refugees in this category home by July 1. Those remaining -- families with children -- will be ordered to leave starting in the middle of the year.
Berlin, which welcomed around 29,000 refugees, said around 9,000 belonged to the first category who have to leave by July.
Under an agreement signed with with Bosnia last November other German states have already started forcible repatriation.

The United Nations said only 250,000 of the total 2.1 million uprooted Bosnians had returned home by the end of last year, despite the right to return being central to the peace treaty which ended 43 months of war in Bosnia.
Haunted by its own memories of war and its aftermath, Germany had welcomed refugees with enthusiasm, providing shelter and about 1,000 marks ($587) per family per month.

But cash-strapped states decided last October to begin forcing the refugees to leave. Germany took in 400,000 refugees from the former Yugoslavia, more refugees than the rest of the European Union combined.

Berlin said it costs about 500 million marks ($290 million) a year to support its share of the refugees and the city said only 1,267 refugees had returned home of their own accord by the end of February.
The threat of forcible repatriation has driven some refugees to desperate acts such as the hijacking of an Austrian Airlines plane early this year by a knife-wielding Bosnian.
